question: When a TrueHD decode meets an access unit it cannot read, does oadec's concealment keep everything else exactly what and where it was, and what does Dolby's own decoder do there?
method: Two clips of real damage, cut from three major syncs before to three after a damage region verify reports: oadec decode -p 2 with --on-error stop (the behaviour before) and with the default, conceal; oadec decode of the clip from the restart header that ends the damage, as the clean reference for what follows; and Dolby's TrueHD decoder, the dlbtruehddec GStreamer element of the Dolby Reference Player (dlbtruehdparse align-major-sync=false, presentation=8, out-ch-config=21, max-errors=-1), with plc off and on. Dolby's channel output is oadec's scaled by a constant gain, so its alignment is found by least relative error against the clean reference. Then the stored bit-flip campaign of tools/replay_fuzz.py (seed 7, 100 sites) on the repository fixture with the previous build and this one, and tools/old_new.py --decode over the corpus. The clips and outputs are not committed.

oadec_conceal.said: concealed 19 access units with silence (15.8 ms) in 1 region; the first at 0:00:00.303 (access unit 364): bit read out of bounds: 7 bits requested at bit 1919 with 1 available
concealed 31 access units with silence (25.8 ms) in 1 region; the first at 0:00:00.293 (access unit 352): Huffman code without a terminating bit

reading: On both clips the decode used to stop at the first damaged unit (exit 2). Concealed, it writes every unit: silence over exactly the damage region verify reports (19 and 31 units), the units before it as they were, and from the restart header on the same samples as a clean decode, in the same place. Dolby's decoder repeats the last good unit instead -- 18 and 30 times -- and drops one unit, so what follows comes out 40 samples early; its plc property changes nothing on TrueHD. The whole of Coco, which used to stop five minutes in, decodes to its end with 360 units of silence in 7 regions, the 7 regions verify reports for that presentation, unit for unit, and all 59 083 check words hold. In the bit-flip campaign the 12 decodes that stopped now finish with exit 7, verify is unchanged, and the campaign still passes.
